Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) Background: This proposal is requesting the addition of tracks to an existing degree program, the MS in Dietetics. This is being requested because the program is seeking accreditation by its external credentialing agency. We are requesting that the MS degree now has two tracks – one for students completing the accredited program and one for students who are not completing the accredited program. Currently, the degree does not have any tracks. The MS in Dietetics Program has been in existence since 2015. It was created in partnership with Sodexo Dietetic Internship in anticipation of the 2024 entry level 11/28/2021 12/14/2021

2 credentialing requirement which states that all students need a master’s degree with experiential learning to become Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDNs).
Until 2024, a BS degree and an internship that provides experiential learning are required to become a RDN.
This change prompted free-standing internships to partner with universities to meet this new degree requirement.
The University of Rhode Island has successfully worked with Sodexo to provide a master’s degree to its interns for the past 6 years.
We are now formalizing the existing partnership with Sodexo by becoming an accredited Future Graduate Program to meet the Future Education Model (FEM) Standards as outlined by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND).
The FEM requires enhanced integration between the didactic and experiential components as part of the accreditation.
Curriculum changes to meet the new standards were approved in the spring of 2021.
The FEM Program will begin in the fall of 2022.
Students who complete these requirements need to be in a separate track to best manage our accreditation.
In 2018, URI expanded the master’s degree offering to RDNs employed by Sodexo.

This program was requested by Sodexo to help their current RDNs to remain competitive with new graduates entering the workforce with master’s degrees.
RDNs complete the MS degree in a separate cohort, and complete individualized learning experiences instead of the standard experiential learning rotations.
We are requesting a second non-accredited track in the MS in Dietetics degree to allow us to continue to offer the program to these students and to students who are unable to complete the accredited track.
The MS in Dietetics has graduated 217 students as of December 2021.
Rationale: Tracks need to be added to the MS in Dietetics degree to accommodate students affiliated with Sodexo who will not complete the integrated FEM Program.
Track 1 –Integrated Experiential Track 1.
Students completing the integrated program with alignment between experiential learning and didactic material.
This track will be accredited by an external agency.
Track 2 –Individualized Experiential Track 1.
Students who are RDNs employed by Sodexo who are seeking a master’s degree who have already completed the experiential learning component. 2.
Students with experiential learning timing issues.

As the new accreditation requirements are phased in nationwide, it is possible that a small number of students with off-sequence experiential learning may be able to complete this track and sit for the Registered Dietitian exam more quickly.
This is likely a very small number of students. 3.
Students who are unable to complete the experiential component of the FEM track and need a path to degree completion.
This is also likely to be a very small number of students.

There are a total of 17 courses for 37 credits.
All students complete the same 11 core didactic

3 courses. Students in FEM track complete 6 credits of experiential learning that is integrated in the program (NFS 571-576). URI will provide the didactic requirements culminating in a MS degree in Dietetics, and Sodexo will provide the required minimum of 1,000 hours of supervised experiential learning.
Responsibilities of the University of Rhode Island The responsibilities of the University of Rhode Island are to: Provide the Graduate Program Director who meets the requirements of URI and the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND).

The Graduate Program Director will have a 50% time allocation to administer the Graduate Program.
The Graduate Program Director will be responsible for overall management of the Graduate Program following ACEND and URI guidelines.
Provide all of the responsibilities required in the ACEND Standards for a Graduate Program Provide all didactic and practicum courses and course instructors (with the exception of the required “supervised experiential learning” activities to be provided by Sodexo in connection with their own independent, longstanding “Dietetic Internship Program", and as described below) for the Graduate Program culminating in a MS degree in Dietetics and fulfilling ACEND competencies.
A minimum of 75% of the student's time or credit hours will be at the University. ·Confer the degree and maintain student records. 5

· Provide the ACEND verification statement upon Graduate Program completion and maintain these statements indefinitely. ·Assess prior learning of students upon entry to the Graduate Program. · Provide the resources needed to offer the MS degree including administrative/clerical support, IT support, facilities, and student support services.
Develop and market the Graduate Program to potential students.
Share data with the Sodexo co-Director, following FERPA guidelines, to ensure that students successfully complete the experiential learning component of the Graduate Program and to submit accreditation documentation.
Responsibilities of the Sodexo Corporation The responsibilities of the Sodexo Corporation are to: · Provide the Graduate Program Co-Director to manage supervised experiential learning. ·Provide preceptors for supervised experiential learning.
Provide a minimum of 1,0o0 hours of supervised experiential learning activities for each student to meet ACEND competencies.
Provide the resources needed for supervised experiential learning including administrative/clerical support, IT support, facilities, and student support services.
Participate in writing of all ACEND required reports.

Share data with the Graduate Program Director, following FERPA guidelines, to ensure that the Graduate Program can assign grades, confer degrees, and submit accreditation documentation.
Other requirements set forth in the Affiliation Agreement Have full legal and administrative responsibility for all aspects of the supervised experiential learning in dietetics at Sodexo, including responsibility for the collection of all Sodexo tuition and other fees from students, and the maintenance of all appropriate policies and procedures for the experiential learning, and adherence to all applicable laws, including federal and state labor laws, relating to the supervised experiential learning in dietetics at Sodexo.
Exclusivity Agreement dietetics only through the Sodexo supervised experiential learning in dietetics.
Sodexo, however, shall be entitled to train students enrolled in other programs with client partners other than URI.
Financial Management ·Each Collaborating Organization will charge its own tuition and fees, and this money will be used to pay its individual costs.
Neither Collaborating Organization is responsible for paying any costs incurred by the other Collaborating Organization.
Each Collaborating Organization will equally share in the accreditation fees (annual fee and the self-study/site visit fee) of the Graduate Program. 6

Teach Out Process If the Graduate Program is dissolved, or the Affiliation Agreement is terminated by either party, the Collaborating Organizations agree to teach out any students remaining in the Graduate Program so that students can complete the Graduate Program within 150% of the Graduate Program length. FIN 431, Financial Technologies The financial services industries are changing with the emergence of financial technology (FinTech).
This course introduces to the most cutting edge FinTech topics, equip the students with an understanding of the major FinTech products in the market, and provide an overview of the underlying technologies.
Topics may include but are not limited to: blockchain and cryptocurrencies, smart contracting, digital payments, crowdfunding, robo-advising, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing.

FIN 432, Introduction to Financial Data Analytics face-to-face and online (3 crs.) The vast proliferation of data and the increasing complexity of technology continue to transform the way financial markets and the finance industry operate and compete.
This course covers the foundations of finance and statistical methods, and how to perform data analysis in real world financial data using a modern statistical programming environment.
Topics may include but are not limited to: an introduction to Python programming language, the techniques how to evaluate the risk-reward trade off in modern portfolio theory, analyzing time series data, and developing algorithmic trading strategies.
Finally, a short introduction to machine learning applications concludes the course. (Lec. 3) FIN 433, Machine Learning for Finance face-to-face and online (3 crs.) The objective of this course is to present fundamental techniques in machine learning for canonical modeling and decision frameworks in rapidly changing financial technology industry.

Data- centric exercises in Python will be included to reinforce theoretical concepts and demonstrate the application of machine learning technology to financial data analytics. (Lec. 3) Pre: Financial Technologies (FIN 431) and Introduction to Financial Data Analytics (FIN432) with grades of C or better in each course.
